function.mechanism: Releases sulfur dioxide/bisulfite species that inhibit microbial growth and oxidative/enzymatic browning reactions.

adi.basis: EFSA 2016 set a temporary group ADI of 0.7 mg/kg bw/day as SO2 equivalents; EFSA 2022 follow-up withdrew that temporary ADI due to insufficient toxicological database and applied an MOE approach.

efsa.key_finding: Temporary ADI was withdrawn; MOE target of at least 80 indicated concern in high consumers and in sulfite-sensitive subgroups under evaluated scenarios.

fda.notes: GRAS under GMP with restrictions: not used in meats, foods recognized as vitamin B1 sources, or on fruits/vegetables intended to be served/sold raw as fresh.

adi.basis: Group ADI 0-0.7 mg/kg bw (expressed as sulfur dioxide) for sulfites including sodium metabisulfite.

concerns.summary: Sulfites are associated with hypersensitivity reactions in susceptible individuals, especially some asthmatics; this is reflected in FDA sulfite labeling policy and EFSA concern for sulfite-sensitive groups.
A 2025 rat study reported anxiety/depression-like behavior and NO-pathway changes at repeated oral sulfite doses (not directly representative of typical dietary exposure).
Animal and in vitro studies report oxidative stress, organ injury biomarkers, and cytotoxicity at moderate/high experimental concentrations.

no_concern_confirmed: No direct IARC carcinogenic classification for sodium metabisulfite was identified in IARC Monographs classification lists; related sulfur dioxide is Group 3.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA 2016 reported temporary ADI exceedance in some groups; EFSA 2022 withdrew ADI and identified MOE-based concerns; 2025 EFSA exposure update metadata reports highest exposures in toddlers under some scenarios.

risk_assessment.rationale: The additive remains approved/GRAS with defined restrictions, but EFSA withdrew the temporary ADI and identified concern for high consumers and sulfite-sensitive groups; this supports a moderate rather than limited tier.
key_factors: No direct IARC carcinogenic classification for sodium metabisulfite
